haiku-low.q2: The request is refused with the same generic reply. Nothing is written and nothing is sent, because the account already has 3 reset rows in the rolling hour.
haiku-low.q3: A link works for 30 minutes after creation. It ends sooner if it is used, or if a newer link is issued, which marks older unused links as used.
haiku-low.q4: The link is unchanged and still unused. The form shows the reason, and the user can retry with the same link until it expires.
haiku-low.q5: None. All sessions for the account are deleted, including the resetting device's. The user logs in on the login page with the new password.
haiku-low.q6: The worker makes one try plus up to 3 retries with backoff, then logs the failure and deletes the job. The user is not told and gets no email.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is generated and placed in the link inside the queued email job. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored in reset_tokens.
haiku-low.q8: The API hashes the token and looks up the reset_tokens row with that hash. It is valid only if used_at is empty and expires_at has not passed.
haiku-low.q9: It is the count of the account's reset_tokens rows with created_at in the last hour, in that table; no separate counter. Old rows drop out as they age past one hour.
haiku-low.q10: In the same transaction as the new row, every older unused token for that user is marked used, so it fails the link check. The rows are kept so they still count toward the limit.
haiku-low.q11: In one transaction: token marked used, new password hash saved in users, and all the account's sessions deleted. The "password changed" email is queued after the commit, as a separate queue write.
haiku-low.q12: The transaction sets used_at only if the token is still unused and unexpired. The second submit changes no row, so it rolls back and shows the expired page.

sonnet.q1: They see "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is written and nothing is sent.
sonnet.q2: The count is 3 or more, so it skips to the reply. Nothing is written or sent. They get the same generic reply as any other address.
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes after creation (expires_at). Sooner: it is used, or replaced by a newer link request (older unused tokens are marked used).
sonnet.q4: Unchanged. The form shows the reason, the link is still valid and unused, and the user can retry until it expires.
sonnet.q5: None. All sessions for the account are deleted, including the resetting device. No session is created. The user is redirected to the login page and logs in with the new password.
sonnet.q6: The worker makes one try plus up to 3 retries with backoff. After the last failure it logs the failure and deletes the job. Nobody is told and the user gets no email. The link still works until it expires, and the user can ask again. The failed link still counts toward the limit.
sonnet.q7: The API makes the raw token and puts the link containing it in the queued email job, in the same transaction as the hash row. The worker sends that link. The document flags this as an open question, since the raw token sits in the queue until sent.
sonnet.q8: The API hashes the token from the link (SHA-256) and finds the reset_tokens row. The link is valid if used_at is empty and expires_at has not passed. A valid check also gives the account via user_id. The document does not say how the lookup is done beyond the hash.
sonnet.q9: It is not kept in a counter. It is counted from reset_tokens rows created in the last hour (rolling), and used and replaced rows still count. Old requests drop out when their created_at is more than an hour old.
sonnet.q10: In step 1c, inside the same transaction and before the new row is inserted, every older unused token for that user is marked used (used_at set). The rows stay and still count toward the limit.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: the token's used_at is set, the new password hash is saved in users, and all of the account's sessions rows are deleted. The "password changed" email is queued after the commit, as a separate queue write that is not part of the transaction.
sonnet.q12: In the transaction, used_at is set only if the token is still unused and not expired. If no row changes, that submit rolls back and shows the expired page. So only one submit succeeds.
